[[5:14|A city seated on a mountain cannot be hid|Non potest civitas abscondi supra montem posita]], that is, built in a high place; for it is seen by all, even from far off. So you, the shepherds of others, or prelates of the Church, who are founded upon Christ, the highest mountain, of whom it is said in Daniel that He [[Dan 2:35|became a great mountain|factus est mons magnus]], ought not to hide the wisdom granted to you, nor to lie concealed. For it is written: [[Ecclus 41:17|wisdom that is hid, and a treasure that is not seen, what profit is there in them both?|sapientia enim abscondita, et thesaurus invisus, quæ utilitas in utrisque?]]

paras.t: Deinde idem ostenditur per similitudinem lucernæ. Neque accendunt homines lucernam, et ponunt eam sub modio : id est, quum eam accenderint, non abscondunt accensam communiter, nisi forte ad tempus, ut opportuno tempore ponatur in publico ; sed super candelabrum ponunt eam, ut luceat omnibus qui in domo sunt. Simili modo Deus non illustravit Apostolos tam copioso lumine sapientiæ, ut occultentur, ac lateant, sed totum mundum luce veritatis perfundant.
paras.en: Then the same thing is shown by the likeness of a lamp. [[5:15|Neither do men light a candle and put it under a bushel|neque accendunt lucernam, et ponunt eam sub modio]]; that is, when they have lit it, they do not commonly hide it once lit, unless perhaps for a time, so that at the proper time it may be set out in the open; [[5:15|but upon a candlestick|sed super candelabrum]] they set it, [[5:15|that it may shine to all that are in the house|ut luceat omnibus qui in domo sunt]]. In like manner God did not enlighten the Apostles with so abundant a light of wisdom that they should be hidden and lie concealed, but that they should flood the whole world with the light of truth.

paras.t: Ideo subditur : Sic luceat lux vestra, hoc est virtuosa ac splendida conversatio vestra, coram hominibus, id est, in eorum præsentia manifestetur, fiat, ac pateat, ut videant opera vestra bona, et glorificent Patrem vestrum qui in cœlis est : hoc est, ad hoc seu propter hunc finem opera bona coram aliis facite, ut Pater vester cœlestis glorificetur, laudetur, et justus esse noscatur ab illis per vestræ vitæ sanctitatem. Deus namque per servos perversos inhonoratur, per bonos laudatur : secundum quod Apostolus ait quibusdam, Per vos nomen Domini blasphematur inter gentes. Et per Ezechielem ait Dominus frequenter : Commaculastis nomen meum sanctum ; rursusque, Sanctificabo nomen meum magnum, quod pollutum est per vos inter gentes. Gentiles namque et perfidi, si viderint Christianum in omnibus sancte et irreprehensibiliter conversantem, nonne dicturi sunt, Vera et sancta est lex qua talem instruit vitam, et sanctus dominus cui talis complacet vita ? Si autem conspexerint Christianum scelerate agentem, nonne mox legem Christi derident, et talem esse dominum suspicantur, quales sunt servi ejus? Fideles vero et boni, quum viderint quempiam honeste et sancte viventem, statim gratiam Dei collaudant, Deum in suo ministro atque effectu extollunt, ejusque misericordiam admirantur, dicentes : Mirabilis Deus in Sanctis suis. Non ergo debemus bona coram aliis operari, vel proprias manifestare virtutes, propter propriam laudem, sed ad Dei honorem, et etiam ad proximorum ædificationem; solique Deo debemus velle placere finaliter. Ideo enim dicit Salvator : Attendite ne faciatis justitiam vestram coram hominibus, ut videamini ab illis.
paras.en: Therefore it is added: [[5:16|So let your light shine|Sic luceat lux vestra]], that is, your virtuous and shining manner of life, [[5:16|before men|coram hominibus]], that is, let it be shown, done and made plain in their presence, [[5:16|that they may see your good works, and glorify your Father who is in heaven|ut videant opera vestra bona, et glorificent Patrem vestrum, qui in cælis est]]; that is, do good works before others to this end, or for this purpose, that your heavenly Father may be glorified and praised, and be known by them to be just, through the holiness of your life. For God is dishonoured by perverse servants and praised by good ones, according to what the Apostle says to certain men: [[Rom 2:24|the name of God through you is blasphemed among the Gentiles|Nomen enim Dei per vos blasphematur inter gentes]]. And through Ezechiel the Lord often says: You have defiled My holy name; and again, [[Ezech 36:23|And I will sanctify my great name, which was profaned among the Gentiles|Et sanctificabo nomen meum magnum quod pollutum est inter gentes]] through you. For if the Gentiles and unbelievers see a Christian living holily and blamelessly in all things, will they not say: True and holy is the law that forms such a life, and holy is the Lord whom such a life pleases? But if they behold a Christian acting wickedly, do they not straightway deride the law of Christ, and suspect the Lord to be such as His servants are? The faithful and the good, on the other hand, when they see someone living honourably and holily, at once praise the grace of God, extol God in His minister and in His work, and marvel at His mercy, saying: [[Ps 67:36|God is wonderful in his saints|Mirabilis Deus in sanctis suis]]. We ought not, then, to do good before others, or to display our own virtues, for our own praise, but for the honour of God and also for the edification of our neighbours; and in the end we ought to wish to please God alone. For this is why the Saviour says: [[Matt 6:1|Take heed that you do not your justice before men, to be seen by them|Attendite ne justitiam vestram faciatis coram hominibus, ut videamini ab eis]].

paras.t: Porro sciendum, quod operum bonorum quidam sunt communia, ad quæ communiter obligamur, nec alicujus singularis sanctitatis seu simulationis speciem habent. Talia coram aliis fieri debent. Alia sunt opera singularis devotionis, et gratiæ eminentis. Ista itaque potius occultanda videntur, ne homo ultra modum ab aliis reputetur aut honoretur, et ne speciem simulationis incurrat, aut singularis appareat. Unde non debemus in manifesto pectus specialiter tundere, suspiria magna emittere, manus in cœlum extendere, sed cum generali exterioris hominis apparatu esse contenti, interius vero semper ad præcipuam devotionem anhelare.
paras.en: It should further be known that some good works are common ones, to which we are all bound in common, and which have no appearance of any singular holiness or of pretence. Such works ought to be done before others. Others are works of singular devotion and of eminent grace. These, then, seem rather to be hidden, lest a man be esteemed or honoured by others beyond measure, and lest he incur the appearance of pretence or seem singular. Hence we ought not in public to beat our breast in some special way, to heave great sighs, or to stretch out our hands to heaven, but to be content with the common outward bearing of the outer man, while inwardly always longing for a special devotion.

paras.t: Et quoniam Christus nova documenta intulit mundo, ne quis putaret suam doctrinam esse contrariam documentis Moysis et Prophetarum, subjecit : Nolite putare quoniam, id est quod, veni solvere, id est falsificare, reprobare, destruere, legem Mosaicam, aut Prophetas divinitus inspiratos, quorum aliqui fuerunt gentiles et ante legem, ut Job, Enoch. Non veni solvere illa, sed adimplere. Legem enim Christus implevit, secundum duplicem sensum : Primo, quia quod lex jussit, fecit. Factus est enim sub lege, ut eos qui sub lege erant, redimeret, secundum Apostolum. Etenim secundum legem est circumcisus, in templo oblatus. Secundo, quoniam quod legi defuit, perficiendo supplevit, præceptis legis evangelica consilia adjiciendo. Similiter Christus implevit Prophetas, quia quod illi de ejus incarnatione, doctrina, conversatione, prodigiis, passione, resurrectione et ascensione prædixerunt, verificavit et actu complevit, cetera quoque in die judicii adimplebit. Propter quod ait : Necesse est impleri omnia quæ scripta sunt in lege Moysis et Prophetis et Psalmis, de me.
paras.en: And since Christ brought new teachings into the world, lest anyone should think His doctrine contrary to the teachings of Moses and the Prophets, He added: [[5:17|Do not think that I am come to destroy|Nolite putare quoniam veni solvere]], that is, to falsify, reject, or abolish, [[5:17|the law|legem]] of Moses, [[5:17|or the prophets|aut prophetas]] divinely inspired, some of whom were Gentiles and lived before the law, as Job and Enoch. [[5:17|I am not come to destroy|non veni solvere]] them, [[5:17|but to fulfil|sed adimplere]]. For Christ fulfilled the law in a twofold sense. First, because what the law commanded, He did. For He was [[Gal 4:4|made under the law|factum sub lege]], [[Gal 4:5|That he might redeem them who were under the law|ut eos, qui sub lege erant, redimeret]], according to the Apostle. Indeed He was circumcised according to the law, and offered in the temple. Secondly, because what was lacking to the law He supplied by perfecting it, adding the evangelical counsels to the precepts of the law. Likewise Christ fulfilled the Prophets, because what they foretold of His incarnation, teaching, manner of life, wonders, passion, resurrection and ascension, He made true and fulfilled in act; and the rest He will fulfil on the day of judgment. For this reason He says: [[Luke 24:44|all things must needs be fulfilled which are written in the law of Moses and in the prophets and in the psalms, concerning me|necesse est impleri omnia quæ scripta sunt in lege Moysi, et prophetis, et Psalmis de me]].

paras.t: Denique præcepta legis fuerunt triplicia, scilicet : moralia, utpote præcepta Decalogi. Hæc Christus implevit, secundum quod ait : Si vis ingredi ad vitam, serva mandata. Alia erant cærimonialia, ut circumcisio, discretio ciborum, esus agni paschalis, etc. Quæ certum est Christum observasse. Quum enim de Joanne Baptista prædixerit angelus, Vinum et siceram non bibet; et Petrus post resurrectionem Christi testatus sit, Quia nunquam comedi omne immundum et commune : constat quod Christus quoque servaverit discretionem in cibis. Tertia legis præcepta erant judicialia : et hæc Christus interdum misericorditer relaxavit, tanquam legislator præcipuus. Interdum vero probabile est eum talia observasse. Sed videtur contrarium : nam præcepit sanato, ut tolleret lectum suum in sabbato; sabbato quoque fecit lutum quo oculos cæci nati linivit. Propter quod Judei dixerunt : Non est hic homo a Deo, qui sabbatum non custodit. Respondendum, quod opera corporalia quæ directe ordinabantur ad Dei honorem, licebant in sabbato, sicut ornare templum, offerre sacrificium. Quod autem jussit sanato ferre lectum in sabbato, fuit ad declarationem facti miraculi in quo divina virtus resplenduit. Simili modo fecit lutum ad exhibendum miraculum in quo omnipotentia Dei fuit ostensa. Judæi vero male intellexerunt præceptum de honoratione sabbati, multisque aliis, sicut inferius elucescet.
paras.en: Moreover, the precepts of the law were of three kinds. Some were moral, such as the precepts of the Decalogue. These Christ fulfilled, according to what He says: [[Matt 19:17|if thou wilt enter into life, keep the commandments|Si autem vis ad vitam ingredi, serva mandata]]. Others were ceremonial, such as circumcision, the distinction of foods, the eating of the paschal lamb, etc. It is certain that Christ observed these. For since the angel foretold of John the Baptist, [[Luke 1:15|and shall drink no wine nor strong drink|et vinum et siceram non bibet]], and Peter after Christ’s resurrection testified, [[Acts 10:14|I never did eat any thing that is common and unclean|numquam manducavi omne commune et immundum]], it is clear that Christ too kept the distinction of foods. The third kind of precepts of the law were the judicial ones; and these Christ sometimes mercifully relaxed, as the chief lawgiver, though at other times it is probable that He observed them. But the contrary seems to be the case: for He commanded the man He had healed to take up his bed on the sabbath; and on the sabbath too He made the clay with which He anointed the eyes of the man born blind. For this reason the Jews said: [[John 9:16|This man is not of God, who keepeth not the sabbath|Non est hic homo a Deo, qui sabbatum non custodit]]. It must be answered that bodily works directly ordered to the honour of God were lawful on the sabbath, such as adorning the temple and offering sacrifice. And His commanding the healed man to carry his bed on the sabbath served to make known the miracle that had been done, in which the divine power shone forth. In like manner He made the clay to display a miracle in which the omnipotence of God was shown. But the Jews understood the precept of honouring the sabbath wrongly, as they did many others, as will become clear below.

paras.t: Quod igitur Christus implevit hæc omnia, manifestat, subdendo : Amen quippe dico vobis, donec, id est quousque, transeat cælum et terra, id est usque ad finem seculi, in quo cœlum et terra transibunt, et peribunt, seu esse cessabunt, quantum ad esse accidentale, non quantum ad esse substantiale, hoc est quoad qualitatem, situm, motum, et influentiam, non quoad eorum substantiam : tunc enim mutabuntur in melius, nec habebunt motum et influentiam ut modo; iota unum, hoc est minimum verbum seu minima littera, aut unus apes, id est minima particula, non præteribit a lege, id est, non remanebit non adimpletum, sed erit sicut lex asserit, donec omnia in lege contenta, fiant, seu impleantur. Per hoc autem quod dicit, Donec transeat coelum et terra, iota unum, etc., non datur intelligi, quod postmodum iota prætereat ; sed per hoc quod ait interim non preterire iota unum, insinuat, quod nunquam aliquid ibit incassum, nec erit mendosum, quod continetur in lege. Nam et figuræ atque ministeria legis ac Prophetarum in Evangelio adimplentur. Iota proprie est minima littera Hebraica ; apex vero jam sumitur pro particula littere in summitate litteræ posita ad discernendum.
paras.en: That Christ, then, fulfilled all these things He makes plain by adding: [[5:18|For amen I say unto you, till|Amen quippe dico vobis, donec]], that is, until, [[5:18|heaven and earth pass|transeat cælum et terra]], that is, until the end of the world, when heaven and earth will pass away and perish, or cease to be, as to their accidental being, not as to their substantial being; that is, as to their quality, position, motion and influence, not as to their substance; for then they will be changed for the better, and will not have motion and influence as now; [[5:18|one jot|jota unum]], that is, the least word or the least letter, [[5:18|or one tittle|aut unus apex]], that is, the smallest particle, [[5:18|shall not pass of the law|non præteribit a lege]], that is, shall not remain unfulfilled, but shall be as the law asserts, [[5:18|till all be fulfilled|donec omnia fiant]], that is, until everything contained in the law come to pass or be fulfilled. By His saying, [[5:18|till heaven and earth pass, one jot|donec transeat cælum et terra, jota unum]], etc., we are not given to understand that afterwards a jot will pass away; but by saying that meanwhile not one jot will pass, He suggests that nothing contained in the law will ever go for nothing or prove false. For the figures and ministries of the law and the Prophets too are fulfilled in the Gospel. A jot [iota] is properly the smallest Hebrew letter; a tittle [apex] is here taken for the small stroke placed at the top of a letter to distinguish it.

paras.t: Insuper docet Salvator, in tantum oportere impleri et observari omnia verba legis, ut nee minimum ejus præceptum posset omitti sine damnationis periculo. Qui ergo, hoc est, quum necesse sit omnia illa impleri, ideirco qui solverit, id est, transgressus fuerit, unum de mandatis istis minimis in lege contentis, qua significavi per iota et apicem, et qua statim dicturus sum, videlicet, Non occides, non moechaberis, non perjurabis : quæ licet pertineant ad præcepta Decalogi, tamen minima appellantur, quoniam parvi meriti (comparative loquendo) est ea implere, pertinentque ad imperfectos, rudes, et incipientes. Unde secundum Augustinum, inchoant hominem : faciunt enim declinare a malo. Qui igitur solverit unum de mandatis his minimis, et docuerit sic homines, id est, male et inobedienter vivendo predicaverit aliis, minimus vocabitur, id est, infimus erit et dicetur, quantum ad bona gratie gratum facientis, quamvis interdum sit magnus prælatus, in regno celorum, id est in Ecclesia militanti, de qua dicit Apostolus, loquens de suis discipulis : Hi soli sunt adjutores mei in regno Dei. Talis namque non est in statu salutis et gratiæ, quia prævaricando præceptum, peecat mortaliter; docendo quoque alios quod ipse non facit, imo cujus contrarium facit, gravius peccat, et Deo acceptus non est. Peccatori enim dixit Deus : Quare tu enarras justitias meas ? Propterea itaque minimus judicatur a sanctis et sapientibus viris, quoniam sola fide ad corpus Ecclesiæ pertinet, non per caritatem et opera.
paras.en: Further, the Saviour teaches that all the words of the law must be fulfilled and observed to such a degree that not even its least precept could be omitted without danger of damnation. [[5:19|He therefore|Qui ergo]], that is, since all these things must be fulfilled, therefore he [[5:19|that shall break|solverit]], that is, shall transgress, [[5:19|one of these least commandments|unum de mandatis istis minimis]] contained in the law, which I signified by the jot and the tittle, and which I am about to name at once, namely, Thou shalt not kill, thou shalt not commit adultery, thou shalt not forswear thyself. Although these belong to the precepts of the Decalogue, they are nevertheless called least, because it is of small merit (comparatively speaking) to fulfil them, and they belong to the imperfect, the unformed and beginners. Hence, according to Augustine, they begin a man, for they make him turn aside from evil. He, then, that shall break one of these least commandments, [[5:19|and shall so teach men|et docuerit sic homines]], that is, shall preach to others while living badly and disobediently, [[5:19|shall be called the least|minimus vocabitur]], that is, shall be and be called the lowest, as regards the goods of sanctifying grace [gratia gratum faciens, the grace that makes the soul pleasing to God, as distinct from graces given for the good of others], even though he be at times a great prelate, [[5:19|in the kingdom of heaven|in regno cælorum]], that is, in the Church militant, of which the Apostle says, speaking of his disciples: [[Col 4:11|These only are my helpers, in the kingdom of God|hi soli sunt adjutores mei in regno Dei]]. For such a man is not in the state of salvation and grace, because by transgressing the precept he sins mortally; and by teaching others what he does not do himself, indeed doing the contrary, he sins more gravely, and is not acceptable to God. For [[Ps 49:16|to the sinner God hath said: Why dost thou declare my justices|Peccatori autem dixit Deus: Quare tu enarras justitias meas]]? Therefore he is judged the least by holy and wise men, since he belongs to the body of the Church by faith alone, not by charity and works.

paras.t: Qui autem fecerit et docuerit. Non adjecit, Unum de mandatis istis minimis ; sed absolute affirmat, Qui autem fecerit et docuerit, id est, qui divina præcepta servaverit, et taliter conversando vere instruxerit alios. hic magnus vocabitur, id est, magni meriti erit, in regno cœlorum predicto, imo et in futuro. Nihil enim divinius, secundum Dionysium, quam Deo cooperari in reductione animarum ad suæ beatitudinis fontem. Hine in Daniele legitur : Qui multos erudiunt ad justitiam, quasi stella fulgebunt in perpetuas æternitates.
paras.en: [[5:19|But he that shall do and teach|qui autem fecerit et docuerit]]. He did not add, “one of these least commandments”, but says absolutely, [[5:19|But he that shall do and teach|qui autem fecerit et docuerit]], that is, he who shall keep the divine precepts, and by so living shall truly instruct others, [[5:19|he shall be called great|hic magnus vocabitur]], that is, shall be of great merit, [[5:19|in the kingdom of heaven|in regno cælorum]] just spoken of, and indeed in the one to come. For nothing is more divine, according to Dionysius, than to co-operate with God in leading souls back to the fountain of their blessedness. Hence we read in Daniel: [[Dan 12:3|they that instruct many to justice|qui ad justitiam erudiunt multos]] shall shine [[Dan 12:3|as stars for all eternity|quasi stellæ in perpetuas æternitates]].

paras.t: Quod vero non sufficiat docere, nisi adsit custodia præceptorum, adjecit Salvator : Dico enim vobis discipulis meis, quia nisi abundaverit justitia, id est bona conversatio, vestra plus quam abundat justitia Scribarum et Pharisæorum, hoc est, nisi major fuerit justitia vestra quam illa, non intrabitis in regnum cœlorum, id est in patriam Beatorum. Quod tripliciter accipi potest : Primo, quoniam Scribæ et Pharisæi veraciter docuerunt, sed opera non corresponderunt doctrinæ, prout infra habetur : Super cathedram Moysis sederunt Scriba et Pharisæi : omnia ergo quæcumque dicunt, facite; secundum opera vero eorum nolite facere, dicunt enim et non faciunt. Secundo, quoniam Scribarum et Pharisæorum justitia fuit servare præcepta minima secundum superficialem intellectum eorum, videlicet, non occidere, non mœchari, vitando dumtaxat opera exteriora nefaria, non desideria prava. Per talia quippe præcepta putabant prohiberi opera, non affectum, secundum quod verba sonant. Talis autem justitia non sufficit ad salutem. Huic sensui concordant sequentia, sicut patebit. Tertio accipi potest, quasi dictum ad Apostolos, et prælatos, ac eos qui ex speciali vocatione, professione, seu gradu, ad perfectionem tenentur, ideo eorum non est circa communia languere, quia nec sufficit eis, sed oportet ut vitam aliorum alta puritate transcendant.
paras.en: But that teaching is not enough unless there is also the keeping of the precepts, the Saviour added: [[5:20|For I tell you|Dico enim vobis]], My disciples, [[5:20|that unless your justice|quia nisi abundaverit justitia vestra]], that is, your good manner of life, [[5:20|abound more than that of the scribes and Pharisees|abundaverit … plus quam scribarum et pharisæorum]], that is, unless your justice be greater than theirs, [[5:20|you shall not enter into the kingdom of heaven|non intrabitis in regnum cælorum]], that is, into the fatherland of the Blessed. This can be taken in three ways. First, because the scribes and Pharisees taught truly, but their works did not answer to their teaching, as is said below: [[Matt 23:2|The scribes and the Pharisees have sitten on the chair of Moses|Super cathedram Moysi sederunt scribæ et pharisæi]]: [[Matt 23:3|All things therefore whatsoever they shall say to you, observe and do: but according to their works do ye not. For they say, and do not|Omnia ergo quæcumque dixerint vobis, servate, et facite: secundum opera vero eorum nolite facere: dicunt enim, et non faciunt]]. Secondly, because the justice of the scribes and Pharisees consisted in keeping the least precepts according to their own superficial understanding of them, namely not to kill and not to commit adultery, by avoiding only wicked outward deeds, not evil desires. For they thought that by such precepts deeds were forbidden, not the affection, according to the sound of the words. But such justice is not sufficient for salvation. With this sense what follows agrees, as will appear. Thirdly, it can be taken as said to the Apostles and prelates and to those who by a special calling, profession or rank are bound to perfection: it is not for them, therefore, to be sluggish about common things, since that is not enough for them; rather they must surpass the life of others by a lofty purity.

paras.t: Itaque, quod non sufficiat justitia Scribarum ac Pharisæorum, subjungitur : Audistis quia dictum, id est præceptum a Deo per Moysen, est antiquis, hoc est populo Judæorum egredientium de Ægypto : Non occides ; qui autem occiderit hominem, prætermisso ordine juris, reus erit judicio damnationis, id est, mortem corporalem meretur, et item æternam. Ego autem dico vobis, id est, non solum occidi prohibeo, sed dico, quia omnis qui irascitur fratri suo ira inordinata, rationem obfuscante, reus erit judicio,id est accusatione coram divina justitia. Hoc est tantum dicere : Ego legem non solvo, sed, impleo, expono, atque perficio, et ad perfectam ac sufficientem justitiam doceo ac perduco. In lege enim aperte prohibetur homicidium, quum dicitur, Non occides ; sed lex non exponit perfecte quomodo intelligendum sit illud præceptum. Propterea ego verum intellectum illius pando præcepti, et dico, quod omnis qui irascitur, id est, vindictam desiderat, seu nocumentum inferre proponit, reus est judicio.
paras.en: Accordingly, to show that the justice of the scribes and Pharisees is not enough, it is added: [[5:21|You have heard that it was said|Audistis quia dictum est]], that is, commanded by God through Moses, [[5:21|to them of old|antiquis]], that is, to the people of the Jews coming out of Egypt: [[5:21|Thou shalt not kill. And whosoever shall kill|Non occides: qui autem occiderit]] a man, setting aside the order of law, [[5:21|shall be in danger of the judgment|reus erit judicio]] of condemnation, that is, deserves bodily death, and eternal death as well. [[5:22|But I say to you|Ego autem dico vobis]], that is, I not only forbid killing, but I say [[5:22|that whosoever is angry with his brother|quia omnis qui irascitur fratri suo]] with a disordered anger that darkens the reason, [[5:22|shall be in danger of the judgment|reus erit judicio]], that is, of accusation before the divine justice. This is as much as to say: I do not destroy the law, but I fulfil, expound and perfect it, and I teach and lead men to a perfect and sufficient justice. For in the law murder is openly forbidden when it is said, Thou shalt not kill; but the law does not perfectly explain how that precept is to be understood. Therefore I lay open the true understanding of that precept, and I say that [[5:22|whosoever is angry|omnis qui irascitur]], that is, desires revenge or purposes to do harm, is in danger of the judgment.

paras.t: Est ergo sciendum, quod aliqui Judæorum per præcepta hujusmodi negativa, quibus dicitur, Non oecides, non mœchaberis, non furaberis, æstimabant sola facta vetari, non autem cogitationes et affectiones : unde putabant eas non esse peccata. nisi in opus procederent. Hunc errorem aufert Salvator, insinuans non solum facta, sed etiam motus interiores et verba perversa esse damnatione condigna. Observatio autem præceptorum Decalogi fuit semper ad salutem sufficiens. Si ergo sola facta impia prohiberentur, nemo propter desideria prava, cogitationes, et animi motus, damnaretur : cujus oppositum nunc docet Salvator. Imo ex lege et Prophetis patet oppositum. Scriptum enim est : Væ qui cogitatis inutile; et, Malum vir fratri suo non cogitet in corde suo. Imo per Jeremiam Dominus sepissime ait : Revertimini a cogitationibus vestris pessimis. Ira quoque in veteri Testamento prohibetur Unde in Genesi Jacob : Maledictus (inquit) furor, quia pertinax ; et indignatio, quia dura. Et Joseph ad fratres suos : Ne irascamini, ait, in via. Unde quod dictum est Audistis quia dictum est antiquis, Non occides, quidam exponunt hoc modo : Audistis quia dictum est antiquis per modum interpretationis seu expositionis, Non occides : id est, præceptum de non occidendo interpretabantur de solo facto. Ego autem, corrigendo hujusmodi expositionem, dico vobis, quia omnis qui irascitur, etc.
paras.en: It must be known, then, that some of the Jews reckoned that by negative precepts of this kind, in which it is said, Thou shalt not kill, thou shalt not commit adultery, thou shalt not steal, only deeds were forbidden, and not thoughts and affections; so that they thought these were not sins unless they issued in deed. This error the Saviour removes, suggesting that not only deeds but also inward movements and perverse words are worthy of damnation. Now the observance of the precepts of the Decalogue was always sufficient for salvation. If, then, only wicked deeds were forbidden, no one would be damned for evil desires, thoughts and movements of the mind: the opposite of which the Saviour now teaches. Indeed, the opposite is plain from the law and the Prophets. For it is written: [[Mich 2:1|Woe to you that devise that which is unprofitable|Væ qui cogitatis inutile]]; and, [[Zach 7:10|let not a man devise evil in his heart against his brother|malum vir fratri suo non cogitet in corde suo]]. Indeed through Jeremias the Lord very often says: [[Jer 25:5|Return ye|Revertimini]] [[Jer 25:5|from your wicked devices|a pessimis cogitationibus vestris]]. Anger too is forbidden in the Old Testament. Hence in Genesis Jacob says: [[Gen 49:7|Cursed be their fury, because it was stubborn: and their wrath, because it was cruel|Maledictus furor eorum, quia pertinax: et indignatio eorum, quia dura]]. And Joseph says to his brothers: [[Gen 45:24|Be not angry in the way|Ne irascamini in via]]. Hence some expound the words, [[5:21|You have heard that it was said to them of old|Audistis quia dictum est antiquis]], [[5:21|Thou shalt not kill|Non occides]], in this way: You have heard that it was said to them of old, by way of interpretation or exposition, Thou shalt not kill; that is, they interpreted the precept against killing of the deed alone. [[5:22|But I say to you|Ego autem dico vobis]], correcting this exposition, [[5:22|that whosoever is angry|quia omnis qui irascitur]], etc.

paras.t: Qui autem dixerit fratri suo, id est proximo, Raca, id est, verbum indignantis animi effuderit, tamen confuse et quasi in generali, non certam vituperationem aut contumeliam inferens, sed affectum interioris commotionis per signum seu verbum indignationis aperiens; reus erit consilio, id est tractatu quo investigatur qua pœna torquendus sit quem constat esse damnandum. Qui autem dixerit proximo suo, Fatue, id est, commotionem ira per verbum contumeliosum, manifestam vituperationem designans, effuderit ; reus erit gehennæ ignis, id est poene infernalis. Ecce triplex gradus culpæ, cui correspondet triplex gradus reatus seu pœna. Est enim ira latens in animo : qui notatur, quum dicitur, Qui irascitur. Cujus peena est, mereri judicium. Et est ira prorumpens in vocem indignationis et vituperationis in generali : quod gravius est primo. Cujus pœna est, prolatio sententiæ contra eum : quæ pœna gravior est quam prima. Et est ira in verbum contumeliosum procedens : quod est gravius primis duobus. Cujus pœna est, punitio ignis gehennæ : quæ prædictis poenis est gravior ; ordinantur tamen et tendunt ad eam. Loquitur ergo Salvator de ira prout est mortale peccatum, videlicet ut est ex consensu cum affectu nocendi injuste. Dicere autem, Raca, ex tali ira, est gravius ; dicere vero, Fatue, exstat gravissimum. Secundum Hieronymum, Raca est verbum Hebraicum, significans vacuum vel inane ; et idem dicit Chrysostomus. Augustinus tamen testatur, quod sit vox non significans aliquid determinate, sed solum commoti cordis affectum, cujusmodi sunt interjectiones. Sed hoc facile concordatur, quia secundum Chrysostomum, quamvis significet vacuum seu inane, id est stultum, hic tamen accipitur secundum usum loquentium, scilicet Judæorum, secundum quod quælibet provincia habet aliquod verbum exprobratorium.
paras.en: [[5:22|And whosoever shall say to his brother|Qui autem dixerit fratri suo]], that is, to his neighbour, [[5:22|Raca|raca]], that is, shall pour out a word of an indignant mind, yet vaguely and as it were in general, not uttering a definite reproach or insult, but showing the feeling of inward agitation by a sign or word of indignation, [[5:22|shall be in danger of the council|reus erit concilio]], that is, of the deliberation in which it is examined with what penalty one who is certainly to be condemned should be punished. [[5:22|And whosoever shall say|Qui autem dixerit]] to his neighbour, [[5:22|Thou fool|fatue]], that is, shall pour out the agitation of anger in an insulting word that expresses a plain reproach, [[5:22|shall be in danger of hell fire|reus erit gehennæ ignis]], that is, of the punishment of hell. Behold a threefold degree of fault, to which there answers a threefold degree of guilt or punishment. For there is anger lying hidden in the mind, which is signified when it is said, [[5:22|whosoever is angry|omnis qui irascitur]]; its punishment is to deserve the judgment. And there is anger breaking out into a word of indignation and reproach in general, which is graver than the first; its punishment is the passing of sentence against him, a heavier penalty than the first. And there is anger going on to an insulting word, which is graver than the two before; its punishment is the punishment of the fire of hell, which is heavier than the penalties just mentioned, though these are ordered and tend towards it. The Saviour, then, is speaking of anger as it is a mortal sin, namely as it arises from consent together with the desire to do unjust harm. To say Raca out of such anger is graver; to say Thou fool is gravest of all. According to Jerome, Raca is a Hebrew word meaning empty or void, and Chrysostom says the same. Augustine, however, testifies that it is a word signifying nothing determinate, but only the feeling of an agitated heart, as interjections do. But this is easily reconciled: for, according to Chrysostom, although it signifies empty or void, that is, foolish, it is taken here according to the usage of those speaking, namely the Jews; just as every province has some word of reproach of its own.

paras.t: Circa prædicta inquiritur, quando, et quomodo, et qualiter ira sit. peccatum Quamvis autem hæc quæstio communis sit, habet tamen difficultatem præcipuam propter sanctorum atque catholicorum doctorum contrariam (ut videtur) determinationem. Dicit enim præsenti loco Hieronymus : Definita sententia est, ut ira penitus tollatur. Si enim jubemur verberanti alteram præbere maxillam, et inimicos diligere, et pro persequentibus exorare ; omnis iræ occasio tollitur, quoniam ira viri justitiam Dei non operatur. Sed aliter sonant verba Chrysostomi dicentis hoc loco : Qui ex causa irascitur, reus non est. Nam si ira non fuerit, nee doctrina proficit, nec judicia stant, nec crimina compescuntur. Justa ergo ira, mater est discipline. Itaque non solum non peccat qui cum causa irascitur, sed contra, nisi iratus fuerit peccat, quoniam patientia irrationabilis vitia seminat, negligentiam nutrit, et non solum malos, sed etiam bonos invitat ad malum : quia malus, quamvis incorreptus fuerit, non emendatur; bonus autem, nisi correptus fuerit, perit, quia in corpore prævalet magis malum quam bonum.
paras.en: Concerning what has been said, it is asked when, how and in what way anger is a sin. Although this question is a common one, it has nevertheless a special difficulty because of the (as it seems) contrary determination of the saints and catholic doctors. For Jerome says on this place: “The sentence is settled, that anger is to be taken away altogether. For if we are commanded to offer the other cheek to the one who strikes us, to love our enemies, and to pray for those who persecute us, every occasion of anger is taken away”, since [[Jas 1:20|the anger of man worketh not the justice of God|Ira enim viri justitiam Dei non operatur]]. But the words of Chrysostom, speaking on this place, sound otherwise: “He who is angry with cause is not guilty. For if there were no anger, neither would teaching profit, nor judgments stand, nor crimes be checked. Just anger, then, is the mother of discipline. And so not only does he not sin who is angry with cause, but on the contrary, if he is not angry he sins; for unreasonable patience sows vices, nourishes negligence, and invites not only the wicked but also the good to evil: because the wicked man, though he be not rebuked, is not amended; while the good man, unless he be rebuked, perishes, since in the body evil prevails more than good.”

paras.t: Ad habendam autem hujus quæstionis plenam notitiam, advertendum quod Stoici sive Platonici dixerunt, passiones simpliciter esse malas atque culpabiles, ac animæ morbos. Et horum modum loquendi multi theologi sunt secuti. Peripatetici autem dixerunt passiones esse quosdam motus naturales indifferentes, videlicet nec bonos, nec malos moraliter ex sua ratione, sed fieri bonos, si per rationem moderentur, et malos, si metam rationis excedant. Horum ergo sententiam imitando, quam Augustinus et posteriores communiter imitantur, dicendum, quod ira proprie sumpta, secundum Damascenum, est desiderium ultionis, seu appetitus vindictæ propter injuriam illatam, seu culpam alterius. Hæc autem vindicta bene et male optari potest et exerceri, videlicet secundum rationis censuram et ordinem juris, et item modo opposito. Itaque ira ad rationem se habet dupliciter, scilicet antecedenter, sicque impedit actum rationis, et dicitur ira per vitium. Secundo se habet ad rationem consequenter, prout movetur contra peccata secundum rationis dictamen : quæ dicitur ira per zelum ; et est bona, et actus virtutis moralis quæ appellatur vindicativa. De qua ira dicit Gregorius : Tunc robustius ratio contra peccata erigitur, quum ira subita rationi famulatur. Et denuo : Cavendum summopere est, ne ira quæ ut instrumentum virtutis assumitur, rationi dominetur, ne quasi domina præeat, sed tanquam ancilla ad obsequium parata, a tergo rationis nunquam recedat.
paras.en: To have a full understanding of this question, it must be observed that the Stoics or Platonists said that the passions are simply evil and blameworthy, and diseases of the soul; and many theologians have followed their way of speaking. But the Peripatetics said that the passions are certain natural movements, indifferent in themselves, that is, neither morally good nor evil by their own nature, but that they become good if they are governed by reason, and evil if they exceed the bound of reason. Following, then, the opinion of these, which Augustine and later writers commonly follow, it must be said that anger properly taken is, according to Damascene, the desire of vengeance, or the appetite for revenge on account of an injury inflicted or of another’s fault. Now this vengeance can be desired and exercised well and badly, namely according to the judgment of reason and the order of law, and likewise in the opposite way. So anger stands in a twofold relation to reason. First, as going before it, and so it hinders the act of reason, and is called anger from vice. Secondly, it stands to reason as following it, when it is moved against sins according to the dictate of reason; and this is called anger from zeal, and it is good, and an act of the moral virtue called vindication [vindicativa: the virtue, a part of justice in St Thomas, that rightly seeks the punishment of wrongdoing]. Of this anger Gregory says: “Reason rises up more strongly against sins when anger, roused, serves reason.” And again: “Great care must be taken lest anger, which is taken up as an instrument of virtue, should master reason; lest it go before as a mistress, but rather, like a handmaid ready for service, never depart from behind reason.”

paras.t: Denique moderamen seu ordo rationis circa iram, pensatur dupliciter : Primo, quantum ad id in quod tendit ira, quod est vindicta : quæ si quæratur propter correctionem peccantis, punitionem culpæ, seu conservationem justitiæ, erit ira laudabilis et per zelum. Secundo, quantum ad modum irascendi, videlicet, ne ira immoderate fervescat : sic enim fieret vitiosa, quamvis in finem laudabilem tenderet. Dicendum ergo secundum Thomam, quod ira immoderata ex parte vindictæ optatæ seu irrogatæ, ex suo genere est mortalis, quoniam caritati contrariatur, quæ non irritatur, nec cogitat malum ; contrariatur quoque justitiæ, quia majorem expetit ultionem quam culpa meretur, vel justum est. Potest tamen esse venialis propter parvitatem nocumenti illati, vel propter imperfectionem actus rationem prævenientis. Ira vero immoderata intus, vel foris in signis, ex modo irascendi, non est ex genere suo mortalis, nisi in tantum concrescat, ut faciat hominem a caritate Dei vel proximi sui excidere : quod contingit dum impedit rationem ab eo ad quod tenetur.
paras.en: Further, the governance or order of reason concerning anger is weighed in two ways. First, as to that towards which anger tends, which is vengeance: if this is sought for the correction of the sinner, the punishment of the fault, or the preservation of justice, the anger will be praiseworthy and from zeal. Secondly, as to the manner of being angry, namely that anger should not boil beyond measure; for so it would become vicious, even though it tended to a praiseworthy end. It must be said, then, according to Thomas, that anger that is immoderate on the side of the vengeance desired or inflicted is mortal in its kind, because it is contrary to charity, which [[1 Cor 13:5|is not provoked to anger, thinketh no evil|non irritatur, non cogitat malum]]; it is contrary also to justice, because it seeks a greater revenge than the fault deserves, or than is just. Yet it can be venial because of the smallness of the harm inflicted, or because of the imperfection of an act that comes before reason. But anger that is immoderate inwardly, or outwardly in its signs, by reason of the manner of being angry, is not mortal in its kind, unless it grows so great as to make a man fall from the love of God or of his neighbour; which happens when it hinders the reason from that to which it is bound.

paras.t: Denique præter prædictam acceptionem, sumitur ira adhuc dupliciter, quamvis improprie : Primo, pro sola commotione animi ex imaginatione contrarii : quæ non est grave peccatum. Secundo, pro motu voluntatis, pœnam juste infligentis : et ita dicitur esse in Deo ac angelis. Eo autem modo quo ira laudabilis est, defectus iræ est vitiosus.
paras.en: Besides the sense already given, anger is taken in two further ways, though improperly. First, for the mere agitation of the mind arising from the imagination of something contrary; and this is not a grave sin. Secondly, for the movement of the will inflicting punishment justly; and in this way it is said to be in God and in the angels. And in the way in which anger is praiseworthy, the lack of anger is vicious.

paras.t: Doctores ergo qui iram dicunt omnino vitandam atque culpabilem, accipi possunt de ira rationem præveniente, et dicta per vitium : de qua exponenda sunt auctoritates Scripture quæ iram vituperant. Alii vero loquuntur de ira per zelum, quam bonam esse præsertim hinc constat, quod de Christo scriptum est : Circumspiciens eos cum ira. Hac ira motus est Phinees, et Samson. De ira autem per vitium, Christus jam loquitur.
paras.en: The doctors, then, who say that anger is to be avoided altogether and is blameworthy, can be taken of the anger that comes before reason and is called anger from vice; and the authorities of Scripture that condemn anger are to be expounded of this. The others speak of anger from zeal, which is good, as is clear above all from what is written of Christ: [[Mark 3:5|looking round about on them with anger|circumspiciens eos cum ira]]. With this anger Phinees was moved, and Samson. But it is of anger from vice that Christ is now speaking.

paras.t: Quæritur, quomodo dicens fratri suo, Fatue, mereatur gehennam, quum dicat Apostolus : O insensati Galatæ ! et iterum, Tu, insipiens, quod seminas, etc. Christus quoque ait diseipulis : O stulti et tardi corde ad credendum ! Dicendum, quod quum verba sint note et signa conceptionum animæ, ex ipsa cordis intentione et affectione consideratur culpa in verbis. Dum ergo hujusmodi verba dicuntur non animo calumniandi seu eontemnendi, sed instruendi, aut caritative corripiendi, non est peccatum. Sicque Christus et ejus Apostolus sunt locuti.
paras.en: It is asked how one who says to his brother, Thou fool, deserves hell, when the Apostle says: [[Gal 3:1|O senseless Galatians|O insensati Galatæ]]! and again, [[1 Cor 15:36|Senseless man, that which thou sowest|Insipiens, tu quod seminas]], etc. Christ too says to the disciples: [[Luke 24:25|O foolish and slow of heart to believe|O stulti, et tardi corde ad credendum]]! It must be said that since words are the marks and signs of the conceptions of the soul, the fault in words is judged from the very intention and affection of the heart. When, then, such words are said not with the mind to slander or despise, but to instruct or to correct charitably, it is no sin. And so Christ and His Apostle spoke.

paras.t: Ex hac præinducta doctrina, infert Salvator : Si ergo, id est, quum non liceat irasci fratri, vel dicere ei, Raca, aut, Fatue, idcirco si offers munus tuum, id est oblationem corporalem vel spiritualem quam das Deo vel ejus ministris, non quod Deus ea indigeat, sed quoniam sponte hanc offers in signum quod omnia bona tua a Deo receperis : secundum quod David testatur, Tua, Domine, sunt omnia, et quæ de manu tua accepimus, dedimus tibi ; ac altare materiale in templo ; vel, Ad altare spirituale in anima, quod est fides, secundum Augustinum, vel caritas, secundum Gregorium. Nil enim acceptum est Deo nisi in fide et caritate agatur, et per eas Deo exhibeatur. Et ibi, videlicet in loco et tempore oblationis, recordatus fueris, quia frater, id est proximus, tuus habet aliquid, hoc est justam querelam, adversum te, propter injuriam sibi a te illatam, hoc est, quia ei in aliquo malefecisti. Si enim tu eum offendisti, ipse habet adversum te, non tu contra eum. Si vero ipse te offendit, habes adversus eum ; sed tune sufficit ut ignoscas ei sieut vis tibi a Deo ignosci, nee oportet facere quæ sequuntur : quæ tamen si feceris, opus magnæ perfectionis exhibes, maximamque mercedem acquiris.
paras.en: From this teaching set out beforehand the Saviour infers: [[5:23|If therefore|Si ergo]], that is, since it is not lawful to be angry with one’s brother, or to say to him Raca or Thou fool, therefore, if [[5:23|thou offer thy gift|offers munus tuum]], that is, the bodily or spiritual oblation that thou givest to God or to His ministers (not that God needs these things, but because thou offerest this of thine own accord as a sign that thou hast received all thy goods from God, as David testifies: [[1 Par 29:14|all things are thine: and we have given thee what we received of thy hand|Tua sunt omnia: et quæ de manu tua accepimus, dedimus tibi]]), [[5:23|at the altar|ad altare]], the material altar in the temple; or at the spiritual altar in the soul, which is faith, according to Augustine, or charity, according to Gregory. For nothing is acceptable to God unless it be done in faith and charity and offered to God through them. [[5:23|And there|et ibi]], namely in the place and time of offering, [[5:23|thou remember that thy brother|recordatus fueris quia frater tuus]], that is, thy neighbour, [[5:23|hath anything|habet aliquid]], that is, a just complaint, [[5:23|against thee|adversum te]], on account of an injury done him by thee, that is, because thou hast wronged him in something. For if thou hast offended him, he has something against thee, not thou against him. But if he has offended thee, thou hast something against him; and then it is enough that thou forgive him, as thou wouldst be forgiven by God, and there is no need to do what follows; yet if thou do it, thou showest a work of great perfection and gainest a very great reward.

paras.t: Relinque ibi munus tuum ante altare, id est, inchoatum obsequium seu oblationem suspende vel intermitte, actu aut proposito, quia non esset Deo acceptum, nisi quod subditur, feceris; et vade prius reconciliari fratri tuo, id est, placa et satisfac ei, veniam postulando, et emendationem exhibendo, secundum exigentiam culpæ. Obsequium enim nostrum Deo non placet nisi ex caritate nascatur : quam non habet, imo et contra justitiam agit, qui fratri a se læso non satagit reconciliari et satisfacere. Eundum est autem pedibus corporis, si commode fieri possit, videlicet si frater offensus non longe sit et haberi queat. Alias eundum est pedibus mentis, hoc est desiderio atque proposito, quatenus proponas et optes ei statim satisfacere : quod quia non vales, intendas eum accedere et placare loco et tempore opportunis. In his quoque pensanda est mensura offensæ seu injuriæ proximo irrogatæ, quæ quanto major exstiterit, tanto celerius ac laboriosius conandum est ut reconcilietur offensus. Debemus vero interim munus ante altare relinquere, id est non facere opera bona nisi primo proponamus ire ad fratrem offensum : quod utique propositum exsequi oportet statim quum convenienter fieri poterit.
paras.en: [[5:24|Leave there thy offering before the altar|relinque ibi munus tuum ante altare]], that is, suspend or break off the service or oblation thou hast begun, in act or in purpose, because it would not be acceptable to God unless thou do what follows; [[5:24|and go first to be reconciled to thy brother|et vade prius reconciliari fratri tuo]], that is, appease him and make satisfaction to him by asking pardon and offering amends, as the fault requires. For our service does not please God unless it springs from charity; and he who does not take care to be reconciled to the brother he has hurt, and to make satisfaction to him, does not have charity, and indeed acts against justice. One must go with the feet of the body, if it can conveniently be done, namely if the offended brother is not far off and can be reached. Otherwise one must go with the feet of the mind, that is, by desire and purpose, so that thou purpose and wish to make satisfaction to him at once; and since thou canst not, thou intend to approach and appease him at a fitting place and time. In these things too the measure of the offence or injury done to the neighbour must be weighed: the greater it has been, the more quickly and the more laboriously must one strive that the one offended be reconciled. Meanwhile we ought to leave the gift before the altar, that is, not to do good works unless we first purpose to go to the offended brother; and this purpose must be carried out as soon as it can fittingly be done.

paras.t: Porro, secundum Chrysostomum et Cassianum, ad caritatis perfectionem pracipue pertinet, ut etiam ille qui læsus est, studeat adversarium mitigare, non solum dimittendo illatam injuriam, sed blando sermone cor ejus placando, quatenus de cetero sincerum ad se affectum retineat Sic enim possum alterius quamvis injuriatoris iracundiam, invidiam, perversitatem sanare, ejusque animam a morte culpæ eripere, primo accedendo ad eum, et pacem reformando inter eum et me; et quum non facio hoc, non videor esse perfectus in caritate Christi, qui pro iniquorum salute sanguinem fudit, nec proximi, quem possum a tanto liberare perieulo humiliando me ipsum. Dicit ergo Chrysostomus : Ne dicas : Ille mihi nocuit, ille mihi satisfacere debet, non ego illi. Si pro gloria salutis tuæ jubet te Dominus amicitias facere. tu potius nocitus seu nocumentum perpessus, debes nocentem rogare, ut duplicem gloriam eonsequaris : unam, quia nocitus es ; alteram, quia prior rogasti. Festina ergo inimicum tuum prævenire ad amicitias, ne forte te tardante, ille preveniat ad rogandum, et rapiat de manibus tuis pietatis mercedem. Nam si ille tibi nocuit, et ille te rogat, infruetuosa est amicitia tua. Quam enim justitiam fecisti ante Deum. si rogatus te placaveris ?
paras.en: Further, according to Chrysostom and Cassian, it belongs especially to the perfection of charity that even he who has been hurt should strive to soften his adversary, not only by forgiving the injury done him, but by appeasing his heart with gentle speech, so that he may keep a sincere affection towards him for the future. For in this way I can heal the anger, envy and perversity of another, though he has wronged me, and snatch his soul from the death of guilt, by going to him first and restoring peace between him and me. And when I do not do this, I do not seem to be perfect in the charity of Christ, who shed His blood for the salvation of the wicked, nor in the love of my neighbour, whom I can free from so great a danger by humbling myself. Chrysostom therefore says: “Do not say: He harmed me; he ought to make satisfaction to me, not I to him. If for the glory of thy salvation the Lord commands thee to make friendships, thou who hast been harmed, or suffered the harm, oughtest rather to beg him who harmed thee, that thou mayest gain a double glory: one because thou wast harmed, the other because thou wast the first to ask. Hasten, then, to forestall thine enemy in making friends, lest perhaps, while thou delayest, he forestall thee in asking, and snatch the reward of goodness out of thy hands. For if he harmed thee and he also asks thee, thy friendship is fruitless. For what justice hast thou done before God, if thou art appeased only when asked?”

paras.t: Et tunc veniens, id est, localiter rediens, vel intentionem tuam ad id quod cœperas, revocans, offeres munus tuum, id est, inchoatum Dei obsequium perficies et continuabis, spiritualem. vel corporalem hostiam immolando. Spirituales autem hostiæ sunt devota oratio, Dei laudatio, cordis compunctio, præceptorum impletio.
paras.en: [[5:24|And then coming|et tunc veniens]], that is, returning in place, or calling back thy intention to what thou hadst begun, [[5:24|thou shalt offer thy gift|offeres munus tuum]], that is, thou shalt complete and continue the service of God thou hadst begun, sacrificing a spiritual or bodily victim. Now spiritual victims are devout prayer, the praise of God, compunction of heart, and the fulfilling of the precepts.

paras.t: Insuper infert Salvator aliud documentum ex his quæ de ira inducta sunt. Esto consentiens adversario tuo cito, id est. concordiam fac cum eo quem læsisti, velociter, quoniam perieulum est in mora quum ignores diem et horam, dum es in via cum eo, id est, quum in vita præsenti secum conversaris : quæ vita est via ad patriam, peregrinatio atque exsilium. Ne forte tradat te adversarius judici, id est ne læsus a te, faciat te reum coram Christo, sicque tradat te materialiter, quoniam est occasio et materia propter quam coram Christo culpabilis inveniris : juxta quem modum dracones, abyssi, ignis, grando, et cetera inanimata et irrationabilia, dicuntur Deum laudare; et judex tradat te ministro, id est, Christus det te in manum diaboli, et in carcerem, id est lacum inferni, mittaris, in eternum damnatus, quia non satisfecisti offenso. Amen dico tibi, non exies inde, videlicet de inferno, quasi liberatus (quamvis in die judicii omnes egressuri sint in inferno detenti, rursus gravius retrudendi in eum), donec reddas novissimum quadrantem, id est, pro minima culpa satisfacias : hoc est, nunquam redimeris, quoniam in inferno nulla est satisfactio.
paras.en: Further, the Saviour draws another lesson from what has been brought forward about anger. [[5:25|Be at agreement with thy adversary betimes|Esto consentiens adversario tuo cito]], that is, make peace quickly with him whom thou hast hurt, since there is danger in delay, as thou knowest not the day nor the hour, [[5:25|whilst thou art in the way with him|dum es in via cum eo]], that is, while thou livest with him in the present life, which is the way to the fatherland, a pilgrimage and an exile; [[5:25|lest perhaps the adversary deliver thee to the judge|ne forte tradat te adversarius judici]], that is, lest he whom thou hast hurt make thee guilty before Christ, and so deliver thee materially [that is, not by any act of his own, but by being the matter of thy guilt], since he is the occasion and matter on account of which thou art found guilty before Christ; in the way in which dragons, the deeps, fire, hail and other inanimate and irrational things are said to praise God; [[5:25|and the judge deliver thee to the officer|et judex tradat te ministro]], that is, Christ give thee into the hand of the devil, [[5:25|and thou be cast into prison|et in carcerem mittaris]], that is, into the pit of hell, damned for ever, because thou didst not make satisfaction to the one thou hadst offended. [[5:26|Amen I say to thee, thou shalt not go out from thence|Amen dico tibi, non exies inde]], namely from hell, as one set free (although on the day of judgment all who are held in hell will come out, to be thrust back into it more grievously), [[5:26|till thou repay the last farthing|donec reddas novissimum quadrantem]], that is, till thou make satisfaction for the least fault; that is, thou shalt never be redeemed, since in hell there is no satisfaction.

paras.t: Potest quoque per adversarium intelligi sacra Scriptura, mandatum, seu lex, qua nostris concupiscentiis et propriæ voluntati adversatur, prohibendo quod cupimus. Huic bono adversario consentire debemus, obediendo sacræ Scripturæ, dum sumus cum ea in via, id est, quamdiu vivimus in sæculo isto, in quo verba Dei audimus, et locum merendi ac demerendi habemus; ne forte adversarius iste tradat nos judici, id est, testimonium proferat contra nos, reprobando scelera nostra in conspectu divino. Non autem possumus per adversarium istum intelligere carnem aut dæmonem, quoniam nulli eorum consentire aut concordare debemus.
paras.en: By the adversary can also be understood holy Scripture, the commandment or the law, which opposes our concupiscences and our own will by forbidding what we desire. With this good adversary we ought to agree, by obeying holy Scripture, while we are in the way with it, that is, as long as we live in this world, in which we hear the words of God and have the opportunity of meriting and demeriting; lest perhaps this adversary deliver us to the judge, that is, bear witness against us, condemning our crimes in the sight of God. But we cannot understand by this adversary the flesh or the devil, since we ought neither to agree nor to be at accord with either of them.

paras.t: Deinde Salvator ostendit verum intellectum præcepti negativi prohibentis mœchationem seu adulterium, vel illegitimum concubitum. Audistis quia dictum est, id est divinitus jussum, antiquis, egredientibus ex Ægypto cum Moyse : Non mœchaberis. Ego autem dico vobis, id est, non solum corporalem fornicationem prohibeo : quam Judei putabant dumtaxat hoc prohiberi præcepto, non concupiscentiam interiorem ; imo præceptum quo dicitur, Non concupisces uxorem proximi tui, exposuerunt de signis concupiscentiæ, ut sunt amplexus et oscula, non de concupiscentia intus latente. Dico itaque vobis, quoniam omnis qui viderit mulierem ad concupiscendum eam, id est ad hoc et eo fine, ut concupiscentia feminæ concitetur in eo, jam mœchatus est eam in corde suo, id est, animo seu consensu cum ea fornicatus est, et ipse inordinatus cordis affectus facit eum reum, ac si opere perpetrasset. Deus enim inspicit intima cordis. Concupiscentia itaque qua est cum animi deliberatione atque consensu in delectationem vel opus, est mortale peccatum : quoniam hoc non est solum titillari, sed consentire. Refrenandi sunt ergo sensus exteriores, maxime visus, tactus, auditus, ne mors intret in animam per corporis sui fenestras. Testante quippe Scriptura : Colloquium mulieris quasi ignis exardescit, et propter speciem mulieris multi perierunt. Propter quod ait beatus Job : Pepigi foedus cum oculis meis, ut ne cogitarem quidem de virgine. Unde secundum Gregorium, Non licet videri quod non licet concupisci.
paras.en: Then the Saviour shows the true understanding of the negative precept forbidding adultery [mœchatio], or unlawful intercourse. [[5:27|You have heard that it was said|Audistis quia dictum est]], that is, divinely commanded, [[5:27|to them of old|antiquis]], who came out of Egypt with Moses: [[5:27|Thou shalt not commit adultery|Non mœchaberis]]. [[5:28|But I say to you|Ego autem dico vobis]], that is, I forbid not only bodily fornication, which alone the Jews thought to be forbidden by this precept, and not inward concupiscence; indeed they expounded the precept in which it is said, [[Deut 5:21|Thou shalt not covet thy neighbour’s wife|Non concupisces uxorem proximi tui]], of the signs of concupiscence, such as embraces and kisses, not of the concupiscence that lies hidden within. I say to you, then, [[5:28|that whosoever shall look on a woman to lust after her|quia omnis qui viderit mulierem ad concupiscendum eam]], that is, to this end and with this purpose, that the desire of the woman may be stirred up in him, [[5:28|hath already committed adultery with her in his heart|jam mœchatus est eam in corde suo]], that is, has committed fornication with her in mind or by consent, and the very disorder of the heart’s affection makes him guilty, as if he had carried it out in deed. For God looks upon the inmost things of the heart. Concupiscence, then, that is joined with the deliberation and consent of the mind to the pleasure or to the deed, is a mortal sin; for this is not merely to be tickled, but to consent. The outward senses, therefore, must be reined in, above all sight, touch and hearing, lest death enter into the soul through the windows of its body. For, as Scripture testifies, the [[Ecclus 9:11|conversation burneth as fire|colloquium enim illius quasi ignis exardescit]] of a woman, and [[Ecclus 9:9|many have perished by the beauty of a woman|Propter speciem mulieris multi perierunt]]. For this reason blessed Job says: [[Job 31:1|I made a covenant with my eyes, that I would not so much as think upon a virgin|Pepigi fœdus cum oculis meis, ut ne cogitarem quidem de virgine]]. Hence, according to Gregory, it is not lawful to look upon what it is not lawful to desire.

paras.t: Quod si oculus tuus dexter scandalizat te, erue eum, et projice abs te. Oculus dexter intelligi potest tripliciter : Primo, ipse oculus corporalis. Si ergo iste scandalizat, id est, occasionem peccandi ingerit, et ad concupiscendum inducit, erue eum, non essentialiter, sed quantum ad usum, id est, reprime eum, ne intueatur illicita : quemadmodum in Ecclesiastico legitur, Averte oculos tuos a muliere compta; et in Psalmo, Averte oculos meos ne videant vanitatem. Et projice abs te, id est, separa eum a te, quantum ad usum illicitum, non quantum ad organum. Juxta hunc sensum dicit Apostolus : Mortificate membra vestra quæ sunt super terram. Et ne hoc male intelligeretur, adjecit quasi exponens se ipsum : Fornicationem, immunditiam, etc., id est, vitia membrorum oceidite. Secundo, per oculum dextrum intelligitur oculus cordis, videlicet intellectus seu consideratio curiosa : quæ abjicienda sunt modo præfato quum scandalum pariunt. Tertio, per oculum dextrum intelligitur quicumque proximus, seu quælibet res adeo cara ut oculus : cujus occasione si ad ruinam peccati inducimur, debemus eam vitare. Cavenda est ergo familiaritas et contactus ejus cujus occasione scandalum patimur. Expedit enim tibi ut pereat,id est, prædicto modo eruatur ac projiciatur abs te, unum membrorum tuorum, videlicet oculus dexter, præsertim dilectus, quam totum corpus tuum, id est earo tua in die judicii, mittatur in gehennam ignis. Potest quoque per corpus intelligi congeries operum, de qua infra dicetur : Si fuerit oculus tuus simplex, totum corpus tuum lucidum erit. Opera autem illorum sequuntur eos. Melius ergo est unius membri vitiosum actum abscindere, quam totius corporis opera bona amittere et damnari.
paras.en: [[5:29|And if thy right eye scandalize thee, pluck it out and cast it from thee|Quod si oculus tuus dexter scandalizat te, erue eum, et projice abs te]]. The right eye can be understood in three ways. First, the bodily eye itself. If, then, this [[5:29|scandalize|scandalizat]] thee, that is, puts before thee an occasion of sinning and leads thee to lust, [[5:29|pluck it out|erue eum]], not in its being but as to its use; that is, restrain it, lest it look upon unlawful things; as we read in Ecclesiasticus: Turn away thine eyes [[Ecclus 9:8|from a woman dressed up|a muliere compta]]; and in the Psalm: [[Ps 118:37|Turn away my eyes that they may not behold vanity|Averte oculos meos, ne videant vanitatem]]. [[5:29|And cast it from thee|et projice abs te]], that is, separate it from thee as to its unlawful use, not as to the organ. In this sense the Apostle says: [[Col 3:5|Mortify therefore your members which are upon the earth|Mortificate ergo membra vestra, quæ sunt super terram]]. And lest this be badly understood, he added, as if expounding himself: [[Col 3:5|fornication, uncleanness|fornicationem, immunditiam]], etc.; that is, kill the vices of the members. Secondly, by the right eye is understood the eye of the heart, namely the understanding, or curious speculation; and these are to be cast away in the manner just described when they give rise to scandal. Thirdly, by the right eye is understood any neighbour, or anything so dear as to be like an eye: if by occasion of it we are led to the ruin of sin, we ought to avoid it. Familiarity and contact, therefore, with anyone through whom we suffer scandal must be shunned. [[5:29|For it is expedient for thee that one of thy members should perish|expedit enim tibi ut pereat unum membrorum tuorum]], that is, be plucked out and cast from thee in the manner described, namely the right eye, especially a beloved one, [[5:29|rather than thy whole body|quam totum corpus tuum]], that is, thy flesh on the day of judgment, [[5:29|be cast into hell|mittatur in gehennam]]. By the body can also be understood the whole mass of one’s works, of which it will be said below: [[Matt 6:22|If thy eye be single, thy whole body shall be lightsome|Si oculus tuus fuerit simplex, totum corpus tuum lucidum erit]]; and, [[Apoc 14:13|For their works follow them|opera enim illorum sequuntur illos]]. It is better, then, to cut off the vicious act of one member than to lose the good works of the whole body and be damned.

paras.t: Et si dextera manus tua scandalizat te, abscide eam, et projice abs te, etc. Sicut de oculo, ita de manu intelligi potest triplieiter, videlicet de manu corporali, de manu interiori, videlicet voluntate, et de quocumque ita dilecto ac utili ut est manus dextera. Quodcumque ergo istorum scandalizaverit te, id est, occasionem peccandi intulerit, abscide illud quantum ad actum, usum, atque affectum immoderatum, quatenus manus corporis a contactu libidinoso, et opere malo cohibeas, voluntatem quoque a pravo desiderio retrahas, proximorum utilitatem ac delectationem, propter bonum honestum, id est animæ tuæ salutem et gratiam, vites. Non enim potest vitare peccata, qui non vitat occasiones peccandi.
paras.en: [[5:30|And if thy right hand scandalize thee, cut it off, and cast it from thee|Et si dextra manus tua scandalizat te, abscide eam, et projice abs te]], etc. As of the eye, so of the hand it can be understood in three ways: of the bodily hand; of the inward hand, namely the will; and of anything as beloved and useful as the right hand. Whichever of these, then, shall have scandalized thee, that is, brought thee an occasion of sinning, cut it off as to its act, its use and its immoderate affection: so that thou keep the hand of the body from lustful touching and from evil work, and draw back the will too from wicked desire, and that thou avoid even the advantage and the pleasure of thy neighbours for the sake of the honest good, that is, the salvation and grace of thy soul. For he cannot avoid sins who does not avoid the occasions of sinning.

paras.t: Præterea Christus corrigit Judæorum errorem circa matrimonium. Dictum est antiquis per Moysen : Quicumque dimiserit uxorem suam, id est, dimittere voluerit, det ei libellum repudii,id est, causam repudiationis scribat et repræsentet, antequam eam dimittat. Libellus repudii, est scriptura continens causam cur uxor dimittitur. Precepit autem Deus per Moysen, non utique uxorem dimittere tanquam in se bonum ac licitum, sed hoc præcepit, ut non dimitteretur nisi dato libello repudii. Sic enim scriptum est : Si acceperit homo uxorem, et non invenerit gratiam ante oculos ejus propter aliquam fœditatem, scribet libellum repudii, quem dabit in manu illius, dimittetque eam. Judæi vero putabant dimissionem uxoris esse simpliciter bonam, jussam ac licitam. ignorantes verba predicta intelligenda esse per modum permissionis, ne majus malum accideret, scilicet, ne Judæi uxores suas odiosas occiderent, ad quod proni fuerunt. Per quem modum etiam permittebantur dare ad usuram extraneis, non autem per modum jussionis. Christus ergo errorem Judæorum excludens, subjecit :
paras.en: Moreover, Christ corrects the error of the Jews concerning marriage. [[5:31|And it hath been said|Dictum est autem]] to them of old through Moses: [[5:31|Whosoever shall put away his wife|Quicumque dimiserit uxorem suam]], that is, shall wish to put her away, [[5:31|let him give her a bill of divorce|det ei libellum repudii]], that is, let him write down and set forth the cause of the repudiation before he puts her away. A bill of divorce is a writing containing the cause why the wife is put away. Now God did not command through Moses that a wife be put away, as though this were good and lawful in itself; but He commanded this, that she should not be put away unless a bill of divorce were given. For thus it is written: [[Deut 24:1|If a man take a wife|Si acceperit homo uxorem]], [[Deut 24:1|and she find not favour in his eyes, for some uncleanness: he shall write a bill of divorce, and shall give it in her hand|et non invenerit gratiam ante oculos ejus propter aliquam fœditatem: scribet libellum repudii, et dabit in manu illius]], and send her away. But the Jews thought that putting away a wife was simply good, commanded and lawful, not knowing that the aforesaid words were to be understood by way of permission, lest a greater evil should happen, namely lest the Jews should kill wives they hated, to which they were prone; in the same way in which they were also permitted to lend at usury to strangers, but not by way of command. Christ therefore, shutting out the error of the Jews, added:

paras.t: Ego autem dico vobis, quia omnis qui dimiserit, id est, a se expulerit, uxorem suam, excepta fornicationis causa, corporalis, vel spiritualis, videlicet idololatriæ, facit eam mœchari, id est, dat ei occasionem adulterandi. Ex quo patet quod divortium sit illicitum, et quod illa toto tempore vitæ suæ maneat uxor prioris mariti, si vixerit. Et qui dimissam duxerit, adulterat, quia alterius viri uxorem sumit in conjugem, cognoscitque eam. Propter utramque autem fornicationem predictam, videlicet adulterium et idololatriam, licet relinquere conjugem seu maritum quantum ad cohabitationem et debiti redditionem. Non tamen oportet nisi in casu. Sunt etiam varii casus in quibus propter fornicationem corporalem non licet relinquere conjugem, scilicet : si mulier ab alio sub specie proprii viri sit cognita, vel si vir eam prostituerit, vel ipse quoque adulter exsistat, etc. His verbis consonant dicta Apostoli ad Corinthios : His qui in conjugio sunt præcipio, non ego, sed Dominus, uxorem a viro suo non discedere : quod si discesserit, manere innuptam, aut viro suo reconciliari ; et vir uxorem non dimittat. De hac materia infra plenius dicetur.
paras.en: [[5:32|But I say to you, that whosoever shall put away|Ego autem dico vobis: quia omnis qui dimiserit]], that is, shall drive from himself, [[5:32|his wife, excepting the cause of fornication|uxorem suam, excepta fornicationis causa]], bodily or spiritual, namely idolatry, [[5:32|maketh her to commit adultery|facit eam mœchari]], that is, gives her occasion of committing adultery. From this it is clear that divorce is unlawful, and that she remains the wife of her former husband for the whole time of her life, if he lives. [[5:32|And he that shall marry her that is put away, committeth adultery|et qui dimissam duxerit, adulterat]], because he takes another man’s wife as his spouse and knows her. Now for either kind of fornication mentioned, namely adultery and idolatry, it is lawful to leave one’s wife or husband as to living together and the rendering of the debt [the marriage debt, that is, conjugal relations]; yet it is not necessary to do so, except in a particular case. There are also various cases in which it is not lawful to leave one’s spouse for bodily fornication: for instance, if the woman has been known by another man under the appearance of her own husband, or if the husband himself has prostituted her, or if he himself is also an adulterer, etc. With these words agree the words of the Apostle to the Corinthians: [[1 Cor 7:10|But to them that are married, not I, but the Lord, commandeth that the wife depart not from her husband|Iis autem qui matrimonio juncti sunt, præcipio non ego, sed Dominus, uxorem a viro non discedere]]. [[1 Cor 7:11|And if she depart, that she remain unmarried or be reconciled to her husband. And let not the husband put away his wife|quod si discesserit, manere innuptam, aut viro suo reconciliari. Et vir uxorem non dimittat]]. Of this matter more will be said below.

paras.t: Iterum audistis quia dictum est antiquis per Moysen : Non perjurabis ; reddes autem Domino juramenta tua : id est, non per idola, neque per elementa, sed per Deum jurabis. Dixit enim : Dominum A Deum tuum timebis, et per nomen ejus jurabis. Hoc Judæi male intellexerunt, putantes sola juramenta mendosa esse prohibita, juramenta quoque injusta et incauta esse servanda. Hunc errorem excludens Salvator, subjunxit :
paras.en: [[5:33|Again you have heard that it was said to them of old|Iterum audistis quia dictum est antiquis]] through Moses: [[5:33|thou shalt not forswear thyself: but thou shalt perform thy oaths to the Lord|Non perjurabis: reddes autem Domino juramenta tua]]; that is, thou shalt swear not by idols nor by the elements, but by God. For He said: [[Deut 6:13|Thou shalt fear the Lord thy God|Dominum Deum tuum timebis]], [[Deut 6:13|and thou shalt swear by his name|ac per nomen illius jurabis]]. This the Jews understood wrongly, thinking that only lying oaths were forbidden, and that unjust and rash oaths too were to be kept. Shutting out this error, the Saviour added:

paras.t: Ego autem dico vobis, non jurare omnino. Secundum Hieronymum, Christus non prohibet jurare per Deum, sed per ea qua subsequuntur, videlicet, Neque per cœlum, etc. Sed quoniam statim subjungitur : Sit autem sermo vester, Est, est ; Non, non : intelligitur, secundum aliquos, Christus etiam juramentum per Deum dissuasisse vel prohibuisse, non quia semper malum atque illicitum sit, sed, ut ait Augustinus, ne per assiduitatem jurandi, incidat homo perjurium. Est quoque alia ratio cur non debeamus jurare sine necessitate, vel magna utilitate, quamvis sint vera qua dicimus : quia hoc cedit ad irreverentiam Dei, quod homo tam leviter, inadvertenter et intimorate assumit tantæ sanctitatis majestatem in testem. Quod autem jurare non sit prorsus illicitum, innotescit per hoc quod Paulus in suis epistolis toties invenitur jurasse, dicendo : Testis est mihi Deus ; et, Testificor coram Deo, etc.
paras.en: [[5:34|But I say to you not to swear at all|Ego autem dico vobis, non jurare omnino]]. According to Jerome, Christ does not forbid swearing by God, but by the things that follow, namely, [[5:34|neither by heaven|neque per cælum]], etc. But since it is added at once, [[5:37|But let your speech be yea, yea: no, no|Sit autem sermo vester, est, est: non, non]], it is understood, according to some, that Christ dissuaded or forbade even an oath by God; not because it is always evil and unlawful, but, as Augustine says, lest by the habit of swearing a man fall into perjury. There is also another reason why we ought not to swear without necessity or great usefulness, even though what we say is true: because it tends to irreverence towards God that a man should so lightly, heedlessly and fearlessly take the majesty of so great a holiness as his witness. But that swearing is not altogether unlawful is made known by the fact that Paul is found to have sworn so often in his epistles, saying: [[Rom 1:9|For God is my witness|Testis enim mihi est Deus]]; and, [[1 Tim 5:21|I charge thee, before God|Testor coram Deo]], etc.

paras.t: Porro, secundum Hieronymum super illud Jeremiæ, Jurabis, Vivit Dominus, in veritate, et judicio, et justitia, tres sunt comites juramenti, videlicet veritas, judicium, et justitia; et quodcumque horum defuerit, juramentum erit illicitum. Imo sic jurans, eo ipso quo jurat, perjurus efficitur, secundum Thomam, quia hæc observare tenetur in quolibet casu. Si enim desit veritas, juramentum est mendax ; si judicium desit, juramentum est temerarium et incautum ; si justitia, iniquum est, leve atque inutile. Veritas itaque ad juramentum ordinata, requiritur ex parte rei de qua juratur; judicium vero seu discretio, ex parte jurantis; Justitia autem, ex parte causæ, ut sit necessitas ad jurandum. Juratio ergo debite circumstantionata, videlicet, ut fiat ex causa necessaria, tune ubi taliter fit et propter congruum finem, non solum est licita, sed et actus virtutis quæ dicitur latria. Qui enim sic jurat, exhibet reverentiam Deo, presupponens eum habere infallibilem veritatem, omniumque certam notitiam, ac universalem providentiam. Unde ait Scriptura : In omni corde suo juraverunt Domino, et invenerunt ; et Psalmista, Laudabuntur omnes qui jurant in eo. Hieronymus quoque affirmat, quod jurans veneratur vel diligit eum per quem jurat.
paras.en: Further, according to Jerome on the words of Jeremias, [[Jer 4:2|And thou shalt swear: As the Lord liveth, in truth, and in judgment, and in justice|Et jurabis: Vivit Dominus in veritate, et in judicio, et in justitia]], there are three companions of an oath, namely truth, judgment and justice; and if any of these is lacking, the oath will be unlawful. Indeed one who swears so becomes a perjurer by the very fact that he swears, according to Thomas, because he is bound to observe these in every case. For if truth is lacking, the oath is lying; if judgment is lacking, the oath is rash and incautious; if justice, it is wicked, light and useless. Truth, then, as ordered to an oath, is required on the side of the thing sworn to; judgment or discretion on the side of the one swearing; and justice on the side of the cause, that there be a necessity for swearing. An oath, therefore, clothed with its due circumstances, namely that it be made from a necessary cause, at a time when it is fitting, and for a fitting end, is not only lawful but also an act of the virtue called latria [the worship due to God alone]. For he who swears in this way shows reverence to God, presupposing that He has infallible truth, certain knowledge of all things, and universal providence. Hence Scripture says: [[2 Par 15:15|for with all their heart they swore|in omni enim corde suo juraverunt]], [[2 Par 15:15|and they found him|et invenerunt]]; and the Psalmist: [[Ps 62:12|all they shall be praised that swear by him|laudabuntur omnes qui jurant in eo]]. Jerome also affirms that he who swears venerates or loves him by whom he swears.

paras.t: Sic ergo intelligenda est littera : Dico vobis non jurare omnino, hoc est non jurare omnibus modis indifferenter, seu ex qualibet causa, sed solum modo jam dicto, videlicet neque per cœlum, quia thronus, id est sedes et habitatio, Dei est. Quamvis enim incircumscriptus immensusque Deus loco nullo claudatur, ibi tamen esse asseritur, ubi operatur et se ipsum ostendit. Quum ergo in cœlo empyreo maxime operetur, illicque facie ad faciem conspiciatur, merito coelum empyreum appellatur thronus ejus. Unde Unigenitus Dei : Ego (inquit) vici, et sedi cum Patre meo in throno ejus.
